Poached Irish Salmon

Served at: Feast of St. Muirgen (Lí Ban the Mermaid)

Serves 4Prep 15 minCook 15-20 min

In honor of St. Muirgen, also known as Lí Ban the Mermaid, whose feast day celebrates her connection to the sea, this Poached Irish Salmon is a fitting and traditional dish. Its delicate flavor and moist texture make it a perfect centerpiece for a celebratory meal, reflecting the bounty of Ireland's waters.

Ingredients

  • 1.5-2 pounds (680-900 g) Irish salmon fillet, skin on or off, pin bones removed
  • 4 cups (950 ml) water or dry white wine (or a mix)
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) fresh lemon juice
  • 1 medium onion, thinly sliced
  • 2-3 sprigs fresh dill
  • 2-3 sprigs fresh parsley
  • 1 bay leaf
  • 1 teaspoon black peppercorns
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste

Method

  1. Rinse the salmon fillet under cold water and pat dry with paper towels. If skin is on, score it lightly a few times.
  2. In a large, wide skillet or shallow pot, combine the water (or wine), lemon juice, sliced onion, dill, parsley, bay leaf, peppercorns, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
  3. Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Reduce heat to low and let it simmer for 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
  4. Carefully place the salmon fillet into the simmering liquid. Ensure the liquid mostly covers the salmon; if not, add a little more water or wine.
  5. Cover the skillet and poach the salmon for 10-15 minutes, or until it is opaque throughout and flakes easily with a fork. The cooking time will vary depending on the thickness of the fillet.
  6. Using a wide spatula, carefully remove the salmon from the poaching liquid and transfer it to a serving platter.
  7. Serve immediately, garnished with fresh dill or parsley, perhaps with a squeeze of fresh lemon.

Tips

  • Do not boil the poaching liquid vigorously; a gentle simmer is key to keeping the salmon moist and tender.
  • The poaching liquid can be strained and reduced slightly to create a light sauce, or used as a base for soup.
  • Serve with boiled new potatoes and steamed green beans for a classic Irish accompaniment.
